quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #10
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 19

questions.question: What does a single dashed yellow line mean?

options.text: Drivers may pass if it is safe.
Both lanes go in the same direction.
Drivers may not pass.
Drivers may pass, even if dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers may pass if it is safe.
questions.explanation: A single dashed yellow line means traffic moves in opposite directions. Drivers may pass if it is safe and will not interfere with oncoming traffic.

questions.question: When may you drive across a dashed white line?

options.text: At any time.
Only during daylight.
When it is safe to change lanes.
Only when passing a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it is safe to change lanes.
questions.explanation: Dashed white lines separate lanes going the same direction. You may cross them to change lanes if it is safe.

questions.question: What does a speed restriction sign show?

options.text: It can be ignored in rain, snow, or ice.
It has a triangular shape.
It is blue with black letters.
A recommended speed for a curve or turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: A recommended speed for a curve or turn.
questions.explanation: Speed restriction signs suggest a safe speed for curves and turns. Even in good weather, follow these signs. Always slow down in rain, snow, or ice.

questions.question: What does a steady green light mean?

options.text: Slow down and prepare to stop.
Stop and check for traffic before going.
You may go through if the road is clear.
You cannot turn right.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may go through if the road is clear.
questions.explanation: A steady green light means you may drive through the intersection if it is clear. You may turn right or left unless a sign says you cannot. Always yield to other vehicles and pedestrians.

questions.question: What must you do when entering a street from a driveway?

options.text: Drive slowly so vehicles and pedestrians can move out of the way.
Honk your horn so vehicles and pedestrians know to move.
Stop and only go when no vehicles or pedestrians are coming.
Ignore pedestrians if there is no sidewalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and only go when no vehicles or pedestrians are coming.
questions.explanation: Always stop before entering the street from a driveway. Yield to all vehicles and pedestrians. Stopping before crossing the sidewalk is required by law.

questions.question: When do you have the right-of-way to turn left?

options.text: A solid green light
A flashing yellow light
A green arrow pointing left
A flashing red light

questions.correctAnswerText: A green arrow pointing left
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you have the right-of-way in that direction. Oncoming traffic must stop for you.

questions.question: How should you enter a highway from an entrance ramp?

options.text: Enter faster than traffic to get ahead.
Enter slowly to avoid other vehicles.
Stop first, then enter slowly.
Speed up to match the traffic speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to match the traffic speed.
questions.explanation: Use the acceleration lane to speed up to match traffic. Signal, look for an opening, and merge safely.

questions.question: What should you do when an emergency vehicle is approaching with flashing lights?

options.text: Try to reach your destination before it catches you.
Keep driving but stay out of its way.
Pull to the side and stop completely.
Stop in the middle of an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the side and stop completely.
questions.explanation: You must yield to all emergency vehicles with sirens or flashing lights. Pull to the right edge and stop. If you are in an intersection, drive through first, then pull over.

questions.question: You find a vehicle defect that affects safe operation. What should you do?

options.text: Fix it as soon as possible.
Fix it when you can afford it.
Drive at slower speeds.
Drive normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fix it as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: Fix any defect that affects safe operation right away. Do not drive the vehicle until it is fixed.

questions.question: What is an inattentive driver?

options.text: A driver who stares off the road or daydreams.
A driver who looks at passengers instead of the road.
A driver who only watches the vehicle ahead.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Stay focused on the road. Do not look at passengers, search your vehicle, read, sightsee, or daydream. Check mirrors and your instruments often. These habits keep you attentive.

questions.question: How does lack of sleep affect your driving ability compared to other things?

options.text: The same way alcohol does.
The same way amphetamines do.
The same way anger does.
The same way driving with teenagers does.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same way alcohol does.
questions.explanation: Fatigue and alcohol affect your driving ability in similar ways. Being awake for 18 hours affects your driving like having a blood alcohol level of 0.05 percent. Being awake for 24 hours affects your driving like having a blood alcohol level of 0.10 percent.

questions.question: What should you do when a driver is tailgating you?

options.text: Move to the right lane if one is available.
If there is no right lane, wait for a clear road ahead and slowly reduce your speed to let them pass.
Never brake suddenly.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: If a driver is tailgating you and a right lane is open, move to it. If no right lane is available, wait until the road ahead is clear, then slowly reduce your speed to encourage them to pass. Never brake suddenly, as this increases the risk of them hitting your vehicle from behind.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Do not drink and drive.
The road is slippery when wet.
The road curves ahead.
A hill is coming.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road is slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road becomes slippery when it is wet.

questions.question: What must you do if you see this sign above your lane?

options.text: You cannot exit the freeway.
You can continue through or exit from your current lane.
You can stay in your lane and continue through.
You must exit the freeway if you stay in your current lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must exit the freeway if you stay in your current lane.
questions.explanation: An "Exit only" sign means that your lane will leave the freeway and form an exit ramp. You can change lanes to continue through the interchange, or you must exit the freeway if you stay in your current lane.

questions.question: What should you do at dusk or on cloudy days?

options.text: Use your four-way flashers.
Use your parking lights.
Do not turn on any lights.
Turn on your headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your headlights.
questions.explanation: At dusk or on cloudy days, turn on your headlights. Use low beams when within 1,000 feet of an oncoming vehicle and when within 500 feet of a vehicle ahead of you. Always use low beams in poor weather.

questions.question: What should a driver do if they see an animal on the road?

options.text: Take no special action.
Honk the horn.
Pass the animal as close as possible.
Be very cautious.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be very cautious.
questions.explanation: Be very cautious when you see an animal on the road. Pass it slowly to avoid startling or scaring it.

questions.question: If a driver is worried, nervous, angry, or crying, what should they do?

options.text: They will drive the same as always.
They can drive faster because they are more alert.
They should calm down and focus on driving before starting the engine.
They should call a friend to talk while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: They should calm down and focus on driving before starting the engine.
questions.explanation: Strong emotions like worry, anger, or sadness can distract you from driving. Take time to calm down and get focused before you start driving.

questions.question: What lights must you use when driving in the rain?

options.text: Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
Parking lights.
No lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights when driving in rain.

questions.question: What must you do when meeting an oncoming vehicle on a narrow road?

options.text: Pull completely off the road and stop.
Give the other vehicle at least half of the road.
Demand that the other vehicle pull over.
Use high beam headlights so they see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the other vehicle at least half of the road.
questions.explanation: On narrow roads, give vehicles traveling in the opposite direction at least half of the road. Both vehicles need enough space to pass each other safely.

questions.question: Why is a leaky exhaust system dangerous?

options.text: It causes hearing loss.
It causes pollution.
It can cause carbon monoxide poisoning.
It causes poor engine performance.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can cause carbon monoxide poisoning.
questions.explanation: The exhaust system removes harmful gases from your vehicle and keeps them out of the passenger area. A leaky exhaust system allows carbon monoxide gas to enter the vehicle, which is dangerous. Fix any exhaust leaks immediately.

questions.question: If you need to slow down on a slippery road, what should you do first?

options.text: Press your brakes hard.
Release the gas pedal.
Use your parking brake.
Pump your brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: On a slippery road, release the gas pedal first. If you need to slow down more, press gently and steadily on the brake pedal.

questions.question: A funeral procession enters an intersection where you are stopped. What should you do?

options.text: The procession should yield to you.
Let the procession pass after the lead vehicle clears the intersection.
Drive through the intersection before the procession.
Join the procession to go through the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the procession pass after the lead vehicle clears the intersection.
questions.explanation: It is courteous to yield to a funeral procession. Once the lead vehicle passes through the intersection, let the rest of the procession go. Do not cut into the procession.

questions.question: A driver's ability to drive safely can be affected by:

options.text: Alcohol.
Any medication.
Not getting enough sleep.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Safe driving requires the driver to be in good condition. Alcohol, drugs, and drowsiness can all make driving unsafe.

questions.question: As you approach an intersection, the traffic light turns yellow. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to pass before the light turns red.
Brake hard to stop immediately.
Be ready to stop in the middle of the intersection.
Be ready to stop before reaching the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop before reaching the intersection.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means the red light is coming soon. Be prepared to stop safely before the intersection if you can.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
Honk your horn at least three times.
Move back into your lane within 10 feet of the other vehicle.
You do not need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
questions.explanation: Before passing, check your mirrors and blind spots. Use your turn signal before changing lanes. Move back into your lane when you can see the front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
